long_biography.plain_text:
Roman Arkadyevich Abramovich was born in Saratov and rose through commodity trading before Russia’s post-Soviet privatization reshaped his career. In the mid-1990s, he and partners acquired control of oil producer Sibneft through that process. The pivotal 2005 sale of his controlling stake to state-owned Gazprom converted the oil holding into investment capital, while stakes in steelmaker Evraz and nickel producer Norilsk Nickel became prominent parts of his portfolio.

Abramovich also served as governor of Chukotka from 2000 to 2008 and invested heavily in the remote region, an unusual public-service chapter in his business career. Internationally, he became best known after buying Chelsea F.C. in 2003; the club changed ownership in 2022 after nineteen years under him. His wealth remains rooted in the Sibneft transaction and subsequent industrial investments, with Forbes currently identifying steel and investments as its source.
